# local 0010: sdld: a PC-relative byte after another byte with a relocation on the same T line gets a displacement that is 2 too low

- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Link output of sdas390 and sdasrab, which were not built, with the patch. Confirm the 2K page check under Decision, then apply.
- Patch: [local-0010.patch](../../patches/local-0010.patch), commit [`3b4fdee07`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/3b4fdee07d6824a9c82595cbd996f41eb848f9a9). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176, the file below links to `60 FE 20 00 F9`. The `jb` is at address 2 and has three bytes,
so the displacement from address 5 to address 0 is `FB`. With `F9` the instruction jumps to
0xFFFE.

```
        .area   CODE1 (ABS)
        .org    0x0000
        jz      0x0000
        jb      0x00,0x0000
```

It was assembled with `sdas8051 -l -o pcr.asm` and linked with `sdld -nf pcr.lk`. The command file
`pcr.lk` has the lines `-muwx`, `-i pcr.ihx`, `-M`, `pcr.rel`, an empty line, and `-e`.

The assembler writes both instructions to one T line. Each branch target is a field of three
bytes, of which the linker outputs one.

    T 00 00 00 60 00 00 00 20 00 00 00 00
    R 00 00 00 02 F1 07 04 00 00 F1 07 09 00 00

With a label on a line of its own between the two instructions, `sdas8051` begins a new T line
for the `jb`, and the file links to `60 FE 20 00 FB`.

The defect needs a relative branch for which the assembler writes a relocation. `mchpcr` in
`sdas/as8051/i51mch.c` resolves a branch to a label in the area of the branch without one. The
destination therefore has to be an absolute address, a label in another area, or an external
symbol. Hand-written assembly such as `jb _flag, label` or `djnz _count, label` with such a label
is affected.

## Cause

`relr3` in `sdas/linksrc/lkrloc3.c` takes `pc + (rtp - rtofst)` as the address of the field that
it relocates. `rtofst` is the number of bytes in front of the field in the T line that are not
output. `relr3` adds to it after a J11 or J19 relocation, after a pdk relocation, and after a byte
relocation with `R3_BYTX`. For sdas8051, sdas390, sdasstm8, and sdasrab, `outrxb` in
`sdas/asxxsrc/asout.c` writes each byte that has a relocation as `a_bytes` bytes with `R_BYT3` in
the mode, which is the `F1` in the R line above. `relr3` does not add to `rtofst` for the bytes of
such a field that are not output. For each such relocation in front of a field, the address of the
field is too high by `a_bytes - 1`, which is 2 for mcs51 and stm8, and a PC-relative displacement
is too low by that amount. r14093, which set the version for the 4.3.0 release, has these lines.

## Fix

`relr3` adds `a_bytes - 1` to `rtofst` after a byte relocation that has `R_BYT3` and does not have
`R3_BYTX`.

## Decision

`relr3` uses the address in two more places, and the patch changes the result of both.

- The page checks for J11 and J19 relocations compare the destination with the page of the first
  byte of the instruction. With the patch, an `ajmp` after a byte relocation on its T line is
  checked with its own address, as an `ajmp` that is the first relocation of its T line is. At
  0x07FE, `ajmp 0x0100` then links without an error, and `ajmp 0x0900` gets "2K Page relocation
  error". The CPU takes the page from the address of the next instruction, so both results are
  wrong for it. Without the patch, an `ajmp` at 0x07FE after `mov a, d` on its T line got the
  opposite results, because its address was 2 too high. The alternative is to change the 2K check
  in this patch as well, so that it uses the address of the next instruction. That was not tried.
- `relr3` makes the adjustment after its error processing. The offset in an error message for the
  first such byte of a T line is therefore unchanged. For a later byte it is 2 lower with the
  patch and is the address of the byte in front of the byte that is output. For an `sjmp` at 0x22
  after `mov a, d`, it is 0x22 with the patch and 0x24 without it.

sdas390 and sdasrab write this form too. They were not built, and their output was not linked
with the patch.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/relative-branch-reloc.c` executes an `sjmp` after `mov a, _path` and a
`djnz _count, addr` in an absolute area at 0xF800, both to absolute addresses. Without the patch
its assertion fails on r17192 for mcs51-small and mcs51-large-stack-auto, which were the two that
were run. On r17192 with the earlier patches of the series it fails for the six mcs51 variants:
the small, medium, large, and huge models, and `--stack-auto` with the small and large models.
With the patch it passes for the six. On host, stm8, and ucz80 the test does not have an
assertion.

With the patch, the file above links to `60 FE 20 00 FB`. The displacements of `djnz d, 0x0010`,
of `jb b, t` with `t` in another area, and of `sjmp` to an absolute address or to another area
after `mov a, d` are 2 higher than without the patch and correct. A branch after `mov a, #<d`,
whose relocation has `R3_BYTX`, links as before. With sdldstm8, `add a, #d` and `jra 0x8010` at
0x8000 link to `AB 00 20 0A` without the patch and to `AB 00 20 0C` with it.

Of the 4848 object files of the regression suite for mcs51-small, only those of this test have a
PC-relative byte relocation. The mcs51 and stm8 libraries do not have one. With the patch series
of this report up to the patch for local 0001 applied to r17192, the regression suite ran without
a failure for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80. The diagnostics suite ran without a
failure for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

## Related

- The test case of bug #3703 has the two instructions of the file above in front of its `ACALL`.
- With and without the patch, the 2K page check uses the page of the first byte of the
  instruction, as Decision describes.
- `sdld` ends with a segmentation fault after it reports a 2K page error for an `acall` or `ajmp`
  to an absolute address. By the source, `errdmp3` reads `a[rindex]` with `rindex` 0xFFFF for
  the `Defin` line. The patch does not change this.
